card.title: PROOF: the train and make deploy-console each stand aside for the other on the live console, and a same-commit tag reads as released

thread.body:
🧭 routing-verdict: **OPERATOR** — Not code — a deploy, a migration run, a secret.

**Why:** the epic's proof card, routed by the proof-and-demo check off the card itself: the card carries an explicit role label, which says where it goes — no judgement, and no model asked An epic is confirmed by something other than its builder, so the fleet is never sent at this card.

**Where it goes:** Hand-work. **Who handles it there:** operator.
**Marked:** `hand-built`, `no-code` — so the sweep neither dispatches a run nor reports the card as stalled.
This card is **not** dispatched to the fleet: the promoter reads this verdict and leaves it where a person will find it.

**Not proven yet. It can't be proven from the logs, and it needs one operator sitting before 16:42 PT on Tuesday 10-13 (read 07:20 PT, 2026-10-08).**

This proof asks to see the release train and `make deploy-console` meet on the live console and stand aside for each other. I read every train run (126) and every console deployment record from 16:42 PT on 10-06, when the last fix merged, to 06:46 PT today.
- **They have never met.** The operator deployed five times. Each time, the train had either already stepped aside under the older rule for infrastructure changes, or it was idle.
- **No train run met a tag already cut** for its commit.
- **The re-arm fix is live.** DRE-6005 is on the `stable` channel, read 07:10 PT today.

All six observations are recorded as "not observed", each with the offline test that covers the same behavior. They are in draft agent-bureau #3381, `architecture/proofs/two-console-writers-2026-10.md`. I made no deploy, dispatch or tag.

**What finishes it:** about an hour at a terminal. First, meet a deploying train with `make deploy-console`. Then deploy and dispatch the train behind it. The card spells out both steps. A window is coming: at 07:16 PT today the console was four commits behind, so the train owes a release. If 10-13 passes first, the record can only merge if the operator accepts the unobserved rows in a written decision.

🧳 hand-built-migration: label removed (`hand-built`).

**What it read:** `hand-built` was put on this card automatically — applied by Agent-Bureau (set at creation) — and the card is a proof in Backlog.

**The rule it followed:** a proof keeps `no-code` and its lane; the proof dispatch takes it from Hand-work, and nothing about it needs the CEO's mark.

The CEO's rule of 2026-10-07: "Build it and let everyone know when i say built it, I'm saying this is a hand built card." The mark is his alone, so the one-time hand-built migration takes off every one the pipeline applied.

Second read (operator helper), 2026-10-09 10:48–10:55 PT. Record updated on draft PR #3381 (commit 69274513).

**Still not proven: the train and `make deploy-console` have still never met.** Since 06:46 PT on 10-08 the train released the console 17 times (v1.6.346 to v1.6.362), and the operator deployed it none. I read all 72 train runs in that span. None stood aside for an operator, none was refused because App Runner was busy, and none met a tag that was already cut. The live console is v1.6.362, released by the train at 22:18 PT on 10-08.

**What finishes it:** one operator sitting at a terminal before **16:42 PT on Tuesday 10-13**. A train release gives an Act A window. Those came about every hour yesterday, and each lasts about five minutes. Act B starts with the operator's own deploy. Every step is a production deploy, dispatch or tag push, and this helper made none.

Operator session, 2026-10-10 08:04 PT. Not started this morning. The clock: DRE-6007 merged at 16:42 PT on 2026-10-06, so this card's record is due by 16:42 PT on 2026-10-13, three days from now.

Both acts are deliberate collisions of two writers on the live console (a real `make deploy-console` started against a running train, a hand-pushed release tag). Last night that same seam misbehaved for real: at 22:46 PT on 10-09 two train runs started two seconds apart and one rolled the console out and could not tag it (DRE-6573, fixed and merged 00:45 PT today), and at 01:47 PT the backend was killed for memory (DRE-6585, its plans waiting in Green Light). I would rather stage a collision on purpose when the CEO knows it is happening than at 08:00 on a Saturday unannounced. It needs about 40 minutes of attention, no outage is expected, and if the first refusal does not come I stop at once.

Recommendation, for the CEO: one word to go, at a time he picks before Tuesday afternoon; I then run both acts, write the record at `architecture/proofs/two-console-writers-2026-10.md` and open its pull request. It is on his list.

**CEO chose 'add a permission rule', 2026-10-12 ~7:55 AM PT.** Added at 8:00 AM PT to the operator checkout's local Claude settings: allow rules and an auto-mode entry for the hand deploy (`AWS_PROFILE=dreadnought NONINTERACTIVE=1 make deploy-console`), the hand tag commands on `agent-bureau-console-v*` (tag -a, tag -d, push), and reading this exercise's logs. Checked at 8:01 AM PT: the 2:19 AM log now reads (it was refused before). It shows observation 3 again: at 02:19:02 PT on 10-11 the hand deploy met train run 38127842468 (deployment 6993500606, v1.6.411, stage cut) and was refused with `busy: release train run … is deploying the console`, aborted before building or touching AWS, exit 2, with both stacks UPDATE_COMPLETE and both App Runner services RUNNING afterward. `DRY=1 make deploy-console` also ran clean at 8:01 AM PT (would become v1.6.434). Still open: the hand tag (observation 6) and Act B (1, 2, 4), at the next real train console release before Tuesday 4:42 PM PT.

**Sitting 2, Act A and the hand tag: SEEN, 2026-10-12, from one train run** (run 38269272134, deployment 7017444900, agent-bureau-console-v1.6.434, sha 96b0f059a). Evidence: ~/Documents/agent-bureau-tracker/evidence/2026-10-11-collision/sitting2 (A-refusal.log, A-refusal-rollout.log, reads/).

Reads straight after: newest record still 7017444900 by github-actions[bot], both stacks UPDATE_COMPLETE (last 04:43/04:48Z), App Runner RUNNING.
- **Observation 6:** annotated tag created locally (cat-file -t: tag; rev-list: 96b0f059a…), pushed 08:22:35 PT, 14 s after roll out began (08:22:21): `* [new tag] agent-bureau-console-v1.6.434`. Tagger is the checkout's git user, agent-bureau-bot[bot].
- **Observation 5, by hand:** 08:22:55 PT both App Runner services read OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS. A second hand deploy at 08:22:56 was refused with `busy: App Runner backend is OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS`, `busy: App Runner web is OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS` and the train line at stage roll out, exit 2.
- **The train's answer:** `==> release: agent-bureau-console-v1.6.434 already exists on origin at 96b0f059a — cut by another writer while this release ran; recording it as released`, `==> DONE -- version agent-bureau-console-v1.6.434 (sha 96b0f059a) deployed at 2026-10-12T15:26:02Z`, `release-train: released dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau console as agent-bureau-console-v1.6.434 at 96b0f05`. Record: cut 08:20:58, build 08:21:06, roll out 08:22:21, verify 08:25:14, success live 08:26:03. Both UPDATE_SERVICE operations SUCCEEDED; both services run the 96b0f05 images.
Still open: Act B (observations 1, 2, 4), the train meeting a hand deploy that started first, before Tuesday 4:42 PM PT. The CEO is told before that daytime deploy starts.
🧹 Reconcile: the 'Backlog' lane is being retired (DRE-4125) and nothing writes to it any more — moved to 'Queued', which is where the work now continues.

**Moved from Queued to Hand-work by the operator session (agent-bureau-3a), 2026-10-13 about 9:05 PM PT.** The 2:47 PM PT drain carried it from Backlog into Queued. It is an operator proof held with `needs-human`, waiting on the operator at a console release, so nothing will ever dispatch it, and in Queued the sweep counted it as a held card on an idle board. That failed agent-bureau's Reconcile every run from 7:32 PM PT. Hand-work is the lane for a person's work.

Operator session, night window 2026-10-24/25. **An Act B attempt at 1:18 AM PT. It released the console, but the two writers did not meet, so observations 1, 2 and 4 are still not observed.** Plain note, not a reading for the record.

- **Owed commit:** `24c8d60b1` (merge of #4172, DRE-7958, at 1:17 AM PT). It changes `console/`, and `git diff --name-only agent-bureau-console-v1.6.605 origin/main -- infra/bin infra/lib infra/cdk.json` came back empty. The three dependency stacks (`cdk diff NetworkStack BureauConsoleData ReleaseStack`) showed no differences at 11:16 PM PT on 10-24.
- **Channel reading for observation 2**, at 1:18:29 AM PT: `gh api repos/dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/compare/30add3b07b7a6546a4a5b604a01d9061089324fc...stable --jq .status` → `ahead` (by 2220).
- **The hand deploy:** `AWS_PROFILE=dreadnought NONINTERACTIVE=1 make deploy-console`, started 1:18:38 AM PT. Its stage record is deployment `7310538091`. It passed `[3/5]` and printed `[4/5]` by 1:20:55 AM PT.
- **The train, dispatched by hand at 1:21:05 AM PT** (`gh workflow run release-train.yml -f surface=console`): run [40176266782](https://github.com/dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau/actions/runs/40176266782). It recorded `deployment 7310563872 (inactive)` with status `release-train-decision/1 no-op ci-pending console` at 1:21:38 AM PT. CI on main for `24c8d60b1` (run 40176046554) was still pending, and the green-at-SHA check runs before the writer check, so the run never reached the deferral. **No deferral, so no re-arm.**
- **The deploy finished:** `DONE -- version agent-bureau-console-v1.6.606 (sha 24c8d60b1) deployed at 2026-10-25T08:26:48Z` (1:26:48 AM PT). Its record `7310538091` reads `success` / `live` at 1:26:52 AM PT. Read at 1:27:32 AM PT: `bureau-console-backend RUNNING`, `bureau-console-web RUNNING`, the console answers, and tag `agent-bureau-console-v1.6.606` is on origin at `24c8d60b1`.

**What Act B actually needs (learned tonight):** the hand dispatch can't produce the deferral while CI on the commit is pending, and once CI is green the train starts by itself. So the hand deploy has to be started about 15 minutes into a console merge's CI (main CI takes about 20–30 minutes), so it is mid-rollout when CI finishes and the train starts on its own. That run then meets the operator's deploy and defers (observation 1), its re-arm fires ten minutes out (observation 2), and the second, interrupted deploy happens while the re-armed run waits (observation 4).

Operator session, 2026-10-25 2:20 AM PT. **Act B stopped for tonight.** No console or infra merge landed on main after 24c8d60b1 between 1:27 and 2:20 AM PT, so there was no owed commit to time a deploy against, and no second hand deploy was made. Observations 1, 2 and 4 stay not observed, and the record (#3381) is unchanged. Act B is left for another night, using the timing in the note above: the hand deploy starts about 15 minutes into a console merge CI run, so the train that CI starts meets it mid-rollout. #3381 stays a draft and keeps needs-human until then.

**Operator decision, written by the operator session (it took none of these readings), 2026-10-29, under the CEO's standing OK of 2026-10-26: observations 1 and 2 are ACCEPTED as seen working, differing only in wording, timing and method.**

The two writers met the way Act B describes at 3:43 AM PT on 2026-10-11, without anyone staging it. Two read-only sessions found it and re-read it on 2026-10-29, as the operator's own `gh` (`smeed652`) and `aws` (profile `dreadnought`). The record on PR #3381 quotes every line below.

**Observation 1, as the card words it:** "**The train defers on the operator** (Act B). The record quotes the train run's receipt line (`deferred: console is being written by an operator deploy (…) — re-arm in 10 minutes`), the run's URL, the `inactive`/`deferred` status on its deployment record, and that the operator's deploy finished and cut its tag with both services `RUNNING`."

What was seen:
- Train run https://github.com/dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau/actions/runs/38132823808 (started by `workflow_run` at 3:41:02 AM PT) printed, stamped 3:43:07 AM PT: `release-train: [console] deferred: console is being written by App Runner backend is OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS; an operator deploy (agent-bureau-console-v1.6.413) opened at 03:37 PT is in flight (deployment 6994300324, stage build) — re-arm in 10 minutes`
- Its deployment record `6994361869` reads `in_progress` at `cut` 3:42:54 AM PT, then `inactive` at `deferred` 3:43:03 AM PT. Its decision record `6994364085` reads `inactive`, `re_arm_at` 3:52:48 AM PT.
- The operator's deploy, record `6994300324` (`smeed652`, no `run_id`), reached `success` at `live` at 3:47:04 AM PT. Tag `agent-bureau-console-v1.6.413` was cut at 3:47:02 AM PT on `247b4370e`.
- CloudFormation stack events: `BackendService` (`AWS::AppRunner::Service`) `UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS` 3:40:32 to `UPDATE_COMPLETE` 3:43:48 AM PT; `WebAppRunnerService` `UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS` 3:44:03 to `UPDATE_COMPLETE` 3:46:47 AM PT. Both were done before the tag.

How it differs, and nothing else does:
1. **Wording.** The line names `App Runner backend is OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS;` first, then the operator deploy. Both were true at the moment the train asked; the card's `console is being written by an operator deploy (…)` is the second clause, and the `— re-arm in 10 minutes` tail is as worded.
2. **Method.** The train was not dispatched by hand after the deploy passed `[3/5]`. It came on its own by `workflow_run` while the operator's record read `build`. The operator deployed a newer commit (`247b437`, which changes `infra/lib`) than the one the train was owed (`27bdd30`, which does not trip the CDK-app deferral). The train still asked who was writing the console, and stood aside.
3. **Method.** "Both services `RUNNING`" was not read at the time and cannot be read now: App Runner keeps 20 operations per service, and the oldest it holds is from 2026-10-27. The stack events above stand in, and show both services finished updating before the tag.
4. **Timing.** Nothing was done at a sitting. Every reading was made on 2026-10-29, as history.

**Observation 2, as the card words it:** "**The re-arm fires** (Act B). Gated on the clause being live for this repo's train, which is a channel reading and not DRE-6005's state: `gh api repos/dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/compare/<DRE-6005's merge sha>...stable --jq .status` answers `ahead` or `identical` (the stub rides `@stable`, DRE-2553). The record quotes that reading first. Then it names the re-armed run the deferral dispatched (the minute in its `Wait until …` job name and its URL) and quotes its decision — a further deferral if the operator was still deploying, and `current` once the operator's tag was in — with `make deploy-lag` read after it."

What was seen:
- The channel reading, at 4:37:12 PM PT on 2026-10-29: `compare/30add3b07b7a6546a4a5b604a01d9061089324fc...stable` answered `ahead 2554 0`, `stable` at `dd25483`. The same compare answered `ahead` at 7:10 AM PT on 2026-10-08 and at 23:18:14 PT on 2026-10-14, either side of the re-arm.
- The re-armed run, https://github.com/dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau/actions/runs/38132947060, dispatched by `github-actions[bot]` at 3:43:06 AM PT. Its job `Wait until 2026-10-11T10:52:48Z` (3:52:48 AM PT) ran from 3:43:28 to 3:52:53 AM PT and printed `release-train: re-armed for 03:52 PT — waiting 552 seconds, then the ordinary decision (green-at-SHA, the spacing, the window, the brake; nothing bypassed)`.
- Its decision, stamped 3:53:42 AM PT: `release-train: no-op dreadnought-foundry/agent-bureau console — console reads current: nothing under console/, infra/ has changed since its newest tag`. Decision record `6994476670`: `code` `current`, `decided_at` 3:53:38 AM PT, `deployed` `agent-bureau-console-v1.6.413`.

How it differs, and nothing else does:
1. **Timing.** The compare reading was made on 2026-10-29, not at a sitting before the re-arm. The readings of 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-14 bracket it, so the clause was live on 2026-10-11. This also covers criterion row 3, "Observation 2 opens with the `compare … stable` reading made at the sitting, so the re-arm is judged against the channel the stub rides and not against DRE-6005's card state.", which the record marks `Met.` on today's reading. There was no sitting for this re-arm.
2. **Method.** `make deploy-lag` was not read after the decision and cannot be read for that moment now. The decision record's `deployed` `agent-bureau-console-v1.6.413` stands in for it.
3. **Timing.** Read on 2026-10-29, as history.

**What stays open.** Observation 4 was not seen and is not accepted. It waits for a production `make deploy-console` started beside a sleeping train run and stopped at `[1/5]`, in the 11 PM to 3 AM PT window.

**Operator decision, written by the operator session, 2026-10-29: criterion row 7, "The CEO closes this card after reading the merged record.", is overtaken by DRE-7773 and ACCEPTED as overtaken.**

DRE-7773 (Done) records the CEO's decision of 2026-10-22, about 10:05 PM PT: "I don't need to close every card." In its words: "A proof card closes when its record merges all-met with the critic's APPROVE ([DRE-5919] already does that), and nothing in a PROOF card or its record asks him to read or close it." It also names this record by number: "Every open record also shows the CEO a last row reading `Open: the CEO's step`", and it teaches the gate to read a closing row like this one as not judged.

So this card closes on its approved record, like every proof card since DRE-7773. Nothing waits on the CEO for row 7. (The stable reader already treats this row as a closing row and does not judge it; this decision is for the person reading the record.)

The "Onboarding Plan" check failed on draft pull request #3381, the proof record for DRE-6008, and failed again on the automatic retry. The branch was cut about 4,480 commits ago, before the onboarding tool existed. The check runs that tool from the branch's own files, so it stopped with "file not found" and reported that the plan could not be computed. Nothing is wrong with the proof record itself, and a retry cannot help. The branch needs to be brought up to date with main, and the check should then pass. That is the fix, and it does not change the proof's content.

One note: this check passes on every current branch, so the pipeline itself is healthy. The gap only shows up on a long-lived branch like this one, which has waited for an operator sitting since early October.

Technical detail: the `plan` job checks out the PR head sha (cf9e4b9), which lacks `scripts/onboarding.py` (404 at that sha; the branch is 7 ahead and 4483 behind main), so `python3 scripts/onboarding.py plan` exits 2 and "Fail on a refusal" reports the plan could not be computed.
